To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the one-dimensional XY model with periodic boundary conditions has an infinite number of stationary points, that these are all saddle points with a single index, and that the Hessian determinants of these saddle points can be computed exactly.

the lattice Landau functional has a unique global maximum and that the random phase XY Hamiltonians with an odd number N of sites and periodic boundary condition have 1 + N/2 local maxima, each of which is a stationary point with index 1/2, and that the Hessian determinant of these stationary points has the value 1/2.

(1) all stationary points are located at the origin, (2) the index of the stationary point is given by the number of negative eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix at the origin, and (3) the index of a stationary point can only change by one when a stationary point is perturbed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stationary points of the functional which appears in lattice gauge fixing and in the XY model.
the stationary point analysis of a lattice gauge fixing functional in the Landau gauge and of the one-dimensional compact U (1) lattice gauge field theory.
the analysis of the stationary points of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian, and their use as a criterion for phase transitions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XY Hamiltonian has a first-order phase transition at an energy which can be computed exactly for all odd lattices.
the lattice Landau functional has no stationary points in the thermodynamic (large lattice) limit.
the XY model does not undergo any phase transition for any value of its coupling constant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found a complete set of stationary points of the lattice Landau functional, including all their indices, which can be used to study the one-dimensional random XY model and the gauge fixing partition functions of compact U(1)-lattices with periodic boundary conditions.
the gauge fixing partition functions of one-dimensional compact U(N) lattice gauge theories with N even are non-vanishing for any value of the gauge coupling and the gauge fixing parameters.

we have found a new, analytic solution of the one-dimensional Landau gauge fixing problem, and that we have derived an exact criterion to determine the existence of phase transition in the one-dimensional random XY model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lattice Landau functional, or the XY Hamiltonian, is not only an important gauge fixing functional in lattice gauge theory but also a very interesting statistical physics model.
the gauge fixing functional has a non-trivial stationary point landscape, which can be understood in terms of the underlying lattice geometry and the gauge fixing condition.
the gauge fixing problem is intimately connected to a phase transition of the XY model.
